evidence_items.source_quote: She has never suffered from filariasis and has no family history of familial lymphedema.

rationale: A 53-year-old morbidly obese female presented with chronic lower limb lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, and erysipelas diagnosed as elephantiasis nostras verrucosa. Filariasis was explicitly evaluated and negated in the narrative ('She has never suffered from filariasis'). The condition is confirmed to be non-filarial elephantiasis, warranting a NEGATIVE label.

evidence_items.source_quote: Extra oral examination revealed no active infection in hands (leprosy) [Figure 2] and legs (elephantiasis) [Figure 3].

The patient was sent for a medical opinion regarding leprosy of the hand and filariasis of the right leg, and no signs of active infections with healed scar were mentioned in the report obtained and no contraindication to carry out the dental procedure was sought from them.

rationale: A 51-year-old female presented with oral myiasis. She reported a remote treated history of leprosy and filariasis. Medical examination explicitly demonstrated no active infection in the legs (elephantiasis) with only a healed scar. Because lymphatic filariasis was solely a historical resolved condition with active infection explicitly ruled out, it does not meet the VPD requirement for active/current disease, leading to a NEGATIVE adjudication.

evidence_items.source_quote: Damage or removal of regional lymph nodes, lymphatic radiation, infection, or tumor invasion, we also exclude the filariasis, that is a direct lymphatic invasion by the parasite Wuchereria bancrofti.

rationale: A 26-year-old male developed lower limb lymphedema after starting sirolimus following renal transplantation. The clinical workup explicitly evaluated and ruled out filariasis ('we also exclude the filariasis, that is a direct lymphatic invasion by the parasite Wuchereria bancrofti'). The definitive diagnosis was sirolimus-induced lymphedema.

evidence_items.source_quote: Chloroform test for chyluria was positive, whereas filarial IgM and IgG antibodies were negative.

rationale: A 51-year-old male presented with chyluria. Testing for filariasis was negative (filarial IgM and IgG antibodies were negative), and an empirical course of diethylcarbamazine produced no improvement. He was cured by silver nitrate endoscopic sclerotherapy, establishing nonparasitic chyluria and ruling out lymphatic filariasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: He also had history of antituberculous and antifilarial treatment with no alleviation of symptoms.

rationale: A 20-year-old male presented with genital elephantiasis. Antifilarial treatment had been administered without improvement, and filariasis was considered in the differential diagnosis. Skin biopsy definitively diagnosed chromoblastomycosis (Fonsecaea pedrosoi) with superimposed erysipelas, ruling out filariasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Filariasis being endemic in Cuddalore district of Tamil Nadu, elephantiasis of external genitalia due to filariasis, besides, lymphogranuloma venereum and granuloma inguinale were also considered.

rationale: A 20-year-old female presented with genital swelling and knife-cut ulcers. Filarial elephantiasis was considered in the differential diagnosis due to local endemicity, but was ruled out in favor of cutaneous/metastatic Crohn's disease, proven by histopathology showing non-caseating granulomas and dramatic therapeutic response to corticosteroids and metronidazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: The possibility of elephantiasis secondary to filariasis was ruled out by a blood smear examination for microfilariae.
evidence_items.test_name: Peripheral blood smear examination for microfilariae

rationale: A 55-year-old female presented with massive vulval swelling. Filarial elephantiasis was explicitly considered in the differential diagnosis and ruled out by negative blood smear examination for microfilariae. Histopathology proved vulval tuberculosis with caseating granulomas, which responded to anti-tubercular therapy. The negative blood smear and definitive alternate diagnosis warrant a NEGATIVE adjudication.
